subject: Acme Analytics — runtime subprocessors & data-use carveout (coordination)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Analytics — runtime subprocessors & data-use carveout (coordination)

Hi team,

Following up from my call with Emma at Acme this morning — they're asking for two DPA/contract exceptions we need to weigh in on before Legal sends the next draft to Contracts: 1) allow a narrow set of runtime subprocessors (observability + metrics export) and 2) a limited "analytics export" carveout for aggregated telemetry to support billing and performance debugging.

I've attached Acme's redline (Acme_DPA_Redline_20260211.pdf) and the runtime subprocessors list they proposed (acme-runtime-subprocessors-20260211.csv). High level: they want to keep exports off by default but retain the right to receive aggregated traces/latency buckets and billing metrics externally. They also want the ability to designate an analytics vendor as a subprocessor for runtime telemetry.

Quick asks:
- Olga: can Legal confirm whether the proposed carveout language can be scoped to aggregated/anonymous telemetry only (no raw prompts or KV cache dumps)?
- Hannah: any security blockers on adding the analytics vendor to our runtime subprocessors list if we require KMS + customer-level telemetry filters?
- David/Product: operationally, what does "aggregated telemetry" look like for you (metrics, traces, examples)? will this change our rollout/feature flags?

Target: get Product + Security sign-off by EOD Friday so I can push the redline to Contracts and keep the ACME procurement timeline intact.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — runtime subprocessors & data-use carveout (coordination)

Thanks Jordan — I reviewed the attached redline. A few legal flags up front:

- The proposed clause as written references "aggregated telemetry" but the definition is broad and could be read to include anything that is pseudonymized. We need a tighter definition: e.g., "non-identifiable, aggregated metrics that do not contain request-level text or user-identifying hashes."

- The subprocessor list needs explicit obligations (SOC2 + encryption-at-rest + keystore restrictions if they will receive runtime telemetry). Naming the analytics vendor isn't enough; we must keep a right to revoke and require contractual change control.

- There's a new "no training" assurance requested by Acme. Legal prefers an explicit clause that prohibits training on customer data unless specifically agreed in writing, with a separate commercial addendum.

If Product/Security can provide concrete operational constraints we can draft tighter language. I'm attaching comments inline in the PDF (Acme_DPA_Redline_20260211.pdf).

- Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — runtime subprocessors & data-use carveout (coordination)

Jordan / Olga — quick security summary from my review:

1) Runtime telemetry export: Acceptable if we enforce strict sampling + aggregation and ban any request/response body or KV/cache content from the export. Must be aggregated at >1,000-user buckets or equivalent differential-privacy protections.

2) Subprocessor onboarding at runtime: We can allow an analytics vendor but only under these conditions:
   - Vendor must be SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) evidence
   - All telemetry encrypted in transit and at rest; customer keys (KMS) required for any persistent export; ephemeral keys for transient streaming permitted only under strong audit controls
   - RBAC so only billing/ops personas can access the exported metrics; no support access to raw telemetry

3) No-training clause: strong preference to keep this standard; any request to train on customer data should be a separate, auditable agreement with opt-ins.

If Legal narrows the "aggregated" definition to exclude any request-level text and we include the KMS + sampling requirements, Security is fine with a limited carveout. I can draft the exact bullet list to insert into the DPA for Product/Legal to sign off.

— Hannah
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — runtime subprocessors & data-use carveout (coordination)

Thanks — product perspective:

- "Aggregated telemetry" for us is: per-route request counts, p50/p90/p99 latency buckets, error counts by category, model selection metrics (model_id, not prompt), and anonymized billing metrics (token counts per tenant). No request or response text, no KV cache dumps, no prompt embeddings.

- Implementation-wise: we currently expose per-tenant aggregated metrics internally and to our billing system. Allowing external exports to an analytics vendor is a new door: we'd need to implement an export pipeline that sits behind a feature flag and enforces transformations (hashing, sampling, enforced encryption). Time to ship: approx 3 sprints (~6 weeks) unless we accept a manual export process for initial setup (hand-off CSVs, monthly cadence).

- Recommended compromise for Acme:
  1) Short-term: legal-approved manual exports (monthly aggregate CSVs) while Product builds export pipeline.
  2) Long-term: automated export with KMS + sampling + audit logs.

If Legal can accept the manual-export interim, we can keep the procurement moving while Product schedules the engineering work. I'll flag this with Engineering for prioritization if we get a firm commitment from Acme on a contract timeline.

— David Kim
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@acme-analytics.com>, Contracts <contracts@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — runtime subprocessors & data-use carveout (coordination)

Emma / Acme Contracts — thanks for the quick turnaround on your redline. Per our internal review we've converged on the following path forward:

1) Scope: the carveout will be limited to "non-identifiable, aggregated telemetry" defined as per-tenant counts, standard latency buckets (p50/p90/p99), error categories, model_id usage counts, and token tallies. No request/response text, no embeddings, and no KV/cache content.

2) Subprocessor onboarding: Acme may designate a single analytics vendor for runtime telemetry exports. That vendor must present SOC2 Type II evidence and sign Redwood's subprocessor addendum. Redwood will retain the right to revoke access on 30 days' notice.

3) KMS & controls: initial exports will be manual (monthly aggregated CSVs) while Product implements an export pipeline with enforced KMS usage, sampling thresholds, and audit logging (target completion ~6 weeks).

4) No-training assurance: Redwood will not use Acme customer data for model training unless a separate commercial agreement is executed.

Next steps:
- Olga: can you incorporate the tightened language and the vendor requirements into the attached PDF and return to Contracts by EOD Monday?
- Hannah: please prepare the exact security bullet list we discussed for insertion (I'll link to it in the DPA).
- David: please confirm the 6-week timeline and whether Product can provide an interim manual export template (CSV schema).

I'll attach the consolidated redline and send a DocuSign envelope once Legal confirms language. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ACME-1892

Thanks all — moving to action.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com)
